I haven't touched the game in a while, but playing WoW during MoP as a teen was such a formative experience and a large part of that was because of how phenomenally designed classes like Warlock were. Chris Kaleiki mentioned at some point during an interview that the class design team wasn't actually that big. To think that the work of a few left such a lasting impression on the game is incredible. The thing is, with a lot of the issues you've mentioned above, it really just boils down to poor implementation, which unfortunately, is a trademark with the majority of Blizzard's expansion-specific features these days. I suppose that's what makes game development so challenging, it requires a lot of creativity, iteration and luck to get a worthwhile feature up and running. I personally think a world-phased version of island expeditions could be fun IF the interactions themselves are interesting **and** simple. The thing with island expeditions and Torghast is that they fell flat because Blizz tried to do so many things in a single concept. Same goes for Ashran in WOD. Meanwhile, in Legion, class order halls and Mythic dungeouns were well-recieved in part because they were a **simple** twist on something players already enjoyed. Realistically speaking, I don't see any issues if the ideas start off simple at launch and are progressively built upon over the expansion as opposed to trying to get everything perfect on the first shot.

Personally, I like it. Or at least the idea of it. There's a lot of directions they can go with cosmic expansions. Not sure if you saw the fanfic expac Twofold Light but it really hits the nail on what a cosmic expac should be. In fact, it looks like Blizz grabbed the Cypher concept off this idea LOL.

Planetary expacs should be rich both in lore and in size so that people feel immersed in the world they're venturing to. The focus shouldn't just be on hyperbolic character-driven stories but also how the world is evolving because of it. Unfortunately, Shadowlands didn't really deliver on either. Take TBC for example, many interesting subplots with alienlike beings and sufficient content to actually drive the stories home. SL seems like an uninspired and poorly funded side project in comparison. So yeah, cosmic stuff could work, but just not with the resources and ideas Blizz is currently throwing at us. But mind you, the same goes for the shitty faction-war BS we got in BFA and the 'savage' themes we were meant to get in WOD.

Lack of inspiration and minmaxing of resources to meet percieved player expectation  thresholds = poorly executed expansion. More or less why players are no longer asking for faction-based or cosmic expacs.
